newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Alfa-Bank sees higher Eurobond volume.
newsitem.headline: Russia Alfa-Bank sees higher Eurobond volume.

text.p: Russia's Alfa-Bank, which finished a road-show for its debut Eurobond on Sunday, has delayed the launch because demand was higher than expected, a top bank official said on Monday.

"Originally we wanted to issue between $75 million and $100 million, but the preliminary portfolio, which reflects interest, far exceeds $200 million," Deputy Chairman Pavel Gorbatsevich told Reuters. "That's why we shall have to change the terms of the issue to higher volume. We may launch tomorrow, but Wednesday is the deadline."
Alfa Russia Finance B.V., Alfa-Bank's Dutch affiliate, will issue Eurobonds led by Goldman Sachs and guaranteed by Alfa-Bank.
Standard & Poor's assigned Alfa-Bank single B credit rating, Moody's B1 and IBCA BB minus.
Alfa-Bank will become Russia's second bank to issue Eurobonds. Last week SBS-Agro issued $250 million worth of paper.
